findings.title: wp-config backup is publicly accessible
findings.description: It contains the database name, user and password.
findings.recommendation: Delete it, then change the database password and the secret keys.
findings.evidence: GET /wp-config.php.bak returned HTTP 200 with matching content

findings.title: Page can be framed (clickjacking)
findings.description: Another site can load this page in an invisible frame and trick visitors into clicking buttons on it.
findings.recommendation: Add X-Frame-Options: DENY (or SAMEORIGIN), or CSP frame-ancestors 'self'.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy
findings.description: Without a CSP, any script injected into a page (XSS) runs with no browser-side limits.

findings.title: WordPress debug.log is publicly accessible
findings.description: Logs reveal file paths, plugin errors and sometimes private data.
findings.recommendation: Delete it and set WP_DEBUG_LOG to a path outside the web root.
findings.evidence: GET /wp-content/debug.log returned HTTP 200 with log lines

findings.title: Directory listing enabled on /wp-content/uploads/
findings.description: Visitors can browse and download everything in the folder.
findings.recommendation: Disable directory listing (Options -Indexes) or add an empty index.php.

findings.title: WordPress is older than the current release series
findings.description: Only the newest WordPress series is officially supported, so older sites may miss security fixes.

findings.title: WordPress user list is public
findings.description: Login names are half of a login; attackers use the list for password guessing.
findings.recommendation: Restrict the REST users endpoint (a security plugin or a small filter does this).

findings.title: Cookie 'wordpress_test_cookie' missing HttpOnly flag
findings.description: JavaScript on the page can read this cookie, so an XSS bug can steal it.
findings.recommendation: Add the HttpOnly attribute to the Set-Cookie header.

findings.title: Cookie 'wordpress_test_cookie' missing SameSite
findings.description: Without SameSite, other sites may trigger requests that carry this cookie (CSRF).

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
findings.description: Browsers may guess file types and run an upload as a script.

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy
findings.description: Full page URLs (which can contain tokens or IDs) may be sent to other sites.

findings.title: Server header reveals a software version
findings.description: Attackers can look up known vulnerabilities for the exact version.
findings.recommendation: Hide the version (Apache: ServerTokens Prod, nginx: server_tokens off).

findings.title: Author archive reveals login names
findings.description: Requesting /?author=1 redirects to a URL containing the user name.
findings.recommendation: Block ?author= requests or redirect them to the home page.

findings.title: WordPress readme.html is reachable
findings.description: It confirms the site runs WordPress and often shows the version.
findings.recommendation: Delete readme.html (it comes back after updates, so block it in the server config).

findings.title: WordPress version is shown in the page source
findings.description: Attackers can match the exact version against known vulnerabilities.

findings.title: xmlrpc.php is enabled
findings.description: It lets attackers try many passwords in a single request.
findings.recommendation: Disable XML-RPC unless you need it (a plugin or one server rule does this).

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy
findings.description: Browser features like camera, microphone and geolocation are not explicitly limited.

findings.title: WordPress detected
findings.description: Knowing the platform tells you which WordPress-specific checks apply.
findings.recommendation: Keep core, themes and plugins updated.

findings.title: Plugins visible in the page source
findings.description: Each plugin is extra attack surface and needs its own updates. Versions were not checked.
findings.recommendation: Remove unused plugins and keep the rest updated.
